doc.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Music videos and draping herself on the piano
summary: Levy recalls her video with Carl Anderson; Wilson does not remember it.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You also did some music videos with Kiyoshi. My recollection is that the – this is when MTV – or VH1 . . .
. . . was starting up, so that we finally had some “jazz” on t.v. in a music video format. Isn’t Forbidden Lover around the time when you finally got a chance to actually lay down on the piano?
Was it Forbidden Lover or was it that song . . .
I’ll Be a Song? No, it was the music video with Carl Anderson. We did two songs from Forbidden Lover.
See, you remember more than I do. I don’t remember. I don’t remember it at all. I remember recording with Carl – singing with Carl, not necessarily recording with him.
It was a studio in Culver City, and the director with the frizzy hair, and Doug Dilge.

What I remember, because I’ve heard you talk about it in interviews, but not related to this video, was the vision you had of draping yourself across a piano, the drama of it all, and for the first time, Nancy Wilson got to do a music video that was all of that.
Okay. I need to see it.
